newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura apologises for arrest of ex-president.
newsitem.headline: Nomura apologises for arrest of ex-president.

text.p: Nomura Securities Co Ltd on Friday apologised for the arrest of its former president Hideo Sakamaki.
The company said in a statement it was surprised to hear of Sakamaki's arrest, which it viewed as very regrettable, and offered its apologies over the incident.
Tokyo prosecutors earlier on Friday arrested Sakamaki in connection with a widening scandal involving suspected illegal payoffs to a racketeer.

Prosecutors said in a statement that Sakamaki, who stepped down as president in March over the scandal and is now an adviser to the giant brokerage, was suspected of violating the Commercial Code and the Securities and Exchange Law by conspiring with three Nomura executives to pay 38.5 million yen ($331,000) to Ryuichi Koike, the "sokaiya" corporate racketeer at the heart of the affair, in March 1995.
